root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted: Schlutter Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 Nbd7

overview: White has played the BDG pawn sacrifice (e4, f3) and recaptured on f3, and Black answers 5...Nbd7, a Schlutter-type development guarding e5 and f6. White is a pawn down but ahead in development with Bf4, Qe2 or Bc4 and Ne5 or kingside attack ideas. Black needs to develop without walking into the quick attacks.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bf4, Qe2, Bc4 and Ne5
Attack the king with g4-g5 or Bc4 and Qe2

black_ideas.idea: Trade pieces and keep the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White d4 against Black pawn majority on the kingside

character.notes: White sacrifices a pawn and plays for fast attack, giving open, tactical positions.

gambit.notes: White is a pawn down and Black can keep it with accurate play.

soundness.notes: Engines favour Black, though the gambit is a practical weapon.

structure.notes: Open lines and files, a free-flowing centre.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom play the BDG.

level.notes: Many opening traps to learn; it is not a beginner choice.
